rv.q: A beautifully portrayed performance and a tribute to April’s Autism acceptance month, this performance promotes connectedness with people like Christopher by conveying his inner life and perspective on navigating the world.

This revival by MadKap Productions, directed by Steve Scott and starring Senn High School student Leo Spiegel as Christopher, is generally sturdy enough to hold one's attention without the technical bells and whistles.
Skokie Theatre's production is proof that different can be a very good thing.
This is a unique bit of theater that some will love and others might say, is it over yet?

cn.t: Critics find this adaptation of Haddon's novel a beautiful and revealing portrayal of a mathematically-gifted autistic teen navigating everyday life, with strong performances that illuminate a unique perspective on the world.
